name: Sokha Meas
story: Sokha learned the art of silk weaving from her grandmother at the age of 10 in Takeo province. After years of practice, she now runs a small workshop employing 12 local women, preserving traditional Khmer weaving techniques that date back over 1,000 years. Her pieces have been exhibited in France and Japan.

name: Dara Chea
story: Dara is a third-generation silversmith from Phnom Penh. He trained under his father and grandfather, mastering the art of repoussé and chasing techniques used to create intricate Angkor-inspired motifs. His workshop in the heart of Phnom Penh attracts visitors from around the world.

name: Sreymom Heng
story: Sreymom is a self-taught artist who discovered her passion for silk painting during the cultural revival movement in Siem Reap. She blends traditional Khmer iconography with contemporary art styles, creating pieces that bridge Cambodia's ancient heritage with modern aesthetics.

name: Bunna Keo
story: Bunna is a third-generation pepper farmer from Kampot who has dedicated his life to reviving the region's legendary pepper industry. After the near-destruction of Kampot pepper during the Khmer Rouge era, his family worked for decades to restore the ancient pepper gardens and obtain GI certification.

name: Virak Pov
story: Virak grew up near the temples of Kampong Thom, where he was inspired by the ancient stone carvings of the Khmer Empire. He apprenticed under a master carver for 7 years before opening his own studio. His work ranges from small souvenirs to large commissioned pieces for hotels and cultural institutions.
